article_title: Gentoo Schedules Chromium Package Removal for October 24 Unless a Volunteer Steps Forward, Citing Maintainer Burnout

content_preview.title: Gentoo Schedules Chromium Package Removal for October 24 Unless a Volunteer Steps Forward, Citing Maintainer Burnout
content_preview.summary: Gentoo has masked its Chromium package and set removal for October 24 unless a volunteer takes over, as maintainers cite long builds, fast releases and a four-release lag.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Gentoo Linux is preparing to remove its source-built Chromium package. According to [Linuxiac](https://linuxiac.com/gentoo-plans-to-drop-chromium-google-chrome-remains-available/), the `www-client/chromium` package is scheduled for removal on October 24 unless a new volunteer steps forward to take over its maintenance, and the package has already been masked to warn users of the planned removal. The decision is a case study in how a volunteer-run distribution handles an upstream pro...

editor_notes.content_quality: News piece of 827 words (range 400-1200), clear structure (Overview, What We Know, Why a Stopgap Was Rejected, What Users Can Do, What We Don't Know, Analysis). Title is 116 chars, within limit. Not human-requested.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read both gzipped snapshots from disk. source-0.html.gz (Linuxiac, Bobby Borisov, October 18, 2026, HTTP 200, full ~5k-char article): confirms www-client/chromium removal scheduled October 24 unless a new volunteer steps forward per an announcement on the Gentoo development mailing list; package already masked; ~6 h build on powerful desktop and 15-16 h on laptop (attributed there to Gentoo's bug tracker); maintainer spends more than six hours of personal time weekly; Gentoo package page lists 151.0.7922.169-r1 vs upstream 155.0.8059.84 'a gap of four major releases' (151->155 = four); Chrome binary remains, Edge/Vivaldi/Opera/Firefox alternatives; community Flathub Chromium. All match. The article attributes the build-time and six-hour figures to Linuxiac, which is accurate. source-1.html.gz (LWN.net, 'Last rites for Gentoo's Chromium package', Joe Brockmeier, October 6, 2026, HTTP 200): snapshot contains the FULL article plus the comment thread (about 89k chars of extracted text), not a paywall stub. Raw text confirms 'Chromium package maintainer Sam James declared last rites for the Chromium package on September 24, after a lengthy conversation in a bug report filed by Roman Zilka' - the announcer is Sam James, NOT Matt Jolly (the WebFetch-summarizer error is not reproduced in the article, which correctly names James). Verbatim quote checks, all pass: Zilka 'a catastrophic 602 known vulnerabilities of all severities' (Sept 9); James 'Chromium is horrible to maintain as a source package. It is easily the package in Gentoo that burns through maintainers the most.'; James 'isn't reliable' (upstream tarball CI); James 'Copying ebuilds works fine until it doesn't'; Szmigiero 'best effort'; Jolly 'We'd lose arm64, ppc64, and the RISC-V overlay' (source continues ' - better to just rip the band-aid off now...', article closes the quote with a period; immaterial); Jolly 'History has shown that one maintainer isn't working' (continues in source with the release-cycle clause, not misrepresented); Jolly 'a commitment to volunteer at least a business day's worth of your free time each week' (source sentence continues 'when you include rebasing patches...'; the article truncates mid-sentence with the period inside the quotes - a minor stylistic imprecision, not a misquote). Non-quoted claims verified: Jolly >6 h/week counting only compilation on a fast PC; release cycle shortened twice since he started maintaining in 2023; new major branch roughly every two weeks, new version weekly; Rust and Go dependencies; at least three maintainers needed; skills C, C++, Go, JavaScript, Rust; Jolly willing to review commits; Flatpak unverified third-party; Chromium not currently a Gentoo binary package; Fedora 154.0.8037.92 vs upstream 154.0.8037.97 published October 1; end of last-rites period October 24; package could be picked up or restored but James wants a sustainable plan. 'Masked' is supported by both (LWN: ebuild is masked after last rites; Linuxiac: already masked). Live re-fetch and independent cross-checks: curl of https://lwn.net/SubscriberLink/1097760/f9747fa7f28b799e/ currently redirects (HTTP 200) to the canonical https://lwn.net/Articles/1097760/ with identical title and content, so the canonical URL is now free to read. Gentoo bug https://bugs.gentoo.org/982204 (not cited, used only for verification) confirms: Zilka's report dated 2026-09-09 with the exact '602 known vulnerabilities' wording; James's 'horrible to maintain' reply; Zilka 'This is ridiculous.' 2026-09-24 06:46 UTC and James 'OK then.' 06:53 UTC; package.mask commit 'Last rite www-client/chromium' by Sam James 2026-09-24; Szmigiero's best-effort request and James's reply; Jolly's 'upwards of six hours' estimate; Valenduc 15 to 16 hours on his laptop. Bug assignee Matt Jolly. No suspicious_patterns in either manifest entry.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every date, number, version string, name and quote traces to the two cited sources and checks out against the raw snapshot text and the live bug tracker. Attribution is correct throughout: James declared last rites (per LWN); Jolly gave the workload, toolchain and three-maintainer comments; Zilka filed the bug. The 'four-release lag' is Linuxiac's own computation (151 vs 155) and is accurately attributed. No fabricated specifics found. Minor nuance: Linuxiac attributes the 15-16 hour laptop figure to the bug tracker, where it is a user's (Valenduc) number; the article attributes it only to Linuxiac, which is accurate.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual. Closing Analysis section is modest and does not overreach (Gentoo is not abandoning Chromium-based browsers; door left open to a larger team). No AI self-reference.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald coverage of Gentoo or this Chromium package removal (grep of articles 2026-09/2026-10 found only unrelated Chrome 155 beta, Git 2.56 and Cloudflare pieces mentioning Chromium/Gentoo in passing). Distinct story.
concerns: SubscriberLink citation: the second source is an LWN SubscriberLink URL. LWN SubscriberLinks are intended to be shared with non-subscribers by subscribers, so citing one is not a circumvention of a paywall, but the URL is a subscriber-issued share token rather than a stable public address, and the page itself carries no explicit terms beyond the standard subscription appeal. The snapshot captured the full article text, so verification was complete. At review time (Oct 19, more than a week after the Oct 6 publication) the canonical URL https://lwn.net/Articles/1097760/ is freely accessible and the SubscriberLink redirects to it, so the canonical URL would have been the better citation and the writer should prefer canonical URLs once available or note the paywall status. This does not affect accuracy and the signed submission is left unmodified; the SubscriberLink currently resolves to the canonical article, so readers are not left with a dead link.
Both cited hostnames (lwn.net line 1280, linuxiac.com line 1107) are already in config/source_allowlist.txt by exact hostname; no allowlist change was needed.
Cosmetic: one Jolly quote is truncated mid-sentence with the closing period inside the quotation marks ('...your free time each week.'); the meaning is unchanged. Not worth a corrections record.

Single-secondary-source pattern: LWN and Linuxiac are both secondary reports of the Gentoo bug and mailing list; Gentoo primary sources are not cited because gentoo.org domains are not allowlisted. All primary facts were independently confirmed against bugs.gentoo.org/982204 during review.
recommendations: Prefer the canonical LWN article URL (lwn.net/Articles/<id>/) once it is free to read, or when the article is not paywalled.
Consider proposing allowlist review for bugs.gentoo.org / gentoo.org primary sources for future distribution-maintenance stories.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-sourced, neutral News piece. All quotes verified verbatim against the raw LWN text and the Gentoo bug tracker, with correct attribution to Sam James, Matt Jolly and Roman Zilka. Integrity checks pass (signature valid, no orphan URLs, 827 words). APPROVE; no corrections required. The pattern-scanner raised no hits.
